title: ADA - Neucom
summary: Neucom's ADA is a reconfigurable neuromorphic processor on a 22nm CMOS process designed to preprocess sparse data from dynamic vision sensors natively. It utilizes interval-coded neural computation via the STICK framework, avoiding frame conversion and reducing preprocessing bottlenecks that consume over 75% of runtime in conventional systems. Benchmarks indicate processing speeds up to 200 million events per second with 5 microsecond latency against standard ARM Cortex-M4 processors. The architecture supports EVT3.0 decoding, denoising, feature extraction for CNNs and SNNs, and hardware attention mechanisms. Software support includes the open-source Axon SDK for Python or C development. As of November 2025, a virtual prototype exists; tapeout is scheduled between Q2-Q3 2026.
tldr: Neucom's ADA processor natively handles sparse event streams from dynamic vision sensors using interval-coded computation to reduce latency and power consumption in robotics and autonomous systems.
evidence: ADA (Asynchronous Dataflow Architecture) is a reconfigurable neuromorphic processor designed to preprocess event streams from dynamic vision sensors.

The chip targets a specific problem in event-based vision: conventional CPUs and GPUs struggle to efficiently handle the sparse, asynchronous data from dynamic vision sensors (DVS), with preprocessing operations consuming over 75% of runtime and power in typical embedded systems.

According to benchmarks in the whitepaper, ADA processes 200 million events per second with 5 microsecond latency, compared to 135,000 events per second with 7.4 microsecond latency on an ARM Cortex-M4 running at 200MHz.
The processor is fabricated on a 22nm CMOS process and designed as IP for integration into larger SoCs via standard digital interfaces.
As of November 2025, ADA is available as a virtual prototype and FPGA implementation for partner evaluation. Tapeout is scheduled for Q2-Q3 2026.
